subject: crab
readings: Top view is XZ panel (round carapace, legs radiate left/right and fore/aft) -> longest extent is left-right leg spread, read from XY & XZ x-axis (0 to 24). ZY panel is the profile (shows fore-aft body length and vertical leg posture).
No head leaf: carapace tapers/fuses directly into eyestalks, no distinct head lobe - counts as trunk only.
carapace center: XY (12,10), ZY (18,11), XZ (x=12, z-tick=10)
claw_R (large chela) tip: XY (22,3) -> dx=+10, dy=+7 (10-3, up since raised); XZ (x=22, z-tick=4) -> dz=+7 (flip: -(4-11))
claw_L tip: XY (2,4) -> dx=-10, dy=+6; XZ (x=2, z-tick=4) -> dz=+7 (mirrored)
leg1_R foot (front walking leg): XY (21,17) -> dx=+9, dy=-7; XZ (x=21, z-tick=8) -> dz=+3
leg2_R foot: XY (23,19) -> dx=+11, dy=-9; XZ (x=23, z-tick=11) -> dz=0
leg4_R foot (rearmost, shorter/closer to body): XY (19,23) -> dx=+7, dy=-13; XZ (x=19, z-tick=18) -> dz=-7
Ground line in ZY/XY panels is at y-tick~22-24 (large tick = low y = negative frame-y), confirming all leg dy are negative from hip to foot as required.
notes: Crab body (cephalothorax) is fused, no protruding head, so carapace counts as trunk only with no head leaf and no tail leaf. Longest extent (24 units) runs left-right through the spread legs/claws, visible fully in XY and XZ panels' x-axis; ZY panel (z horizontal, fore-aft) serves as the profile/side view showing body depth and leg vertical posture. Each of the 5 leg pairs (4 walking + 1 chela/claw pair) is modeled as a 2-segment limb (hip->foot or shoulder->claw) since only proximal attachment and distal tip were clearly legible in the render; intermediate knee bends were inferred from typical crustacean leg anatomy, not separately measured. Attachment points are distributed along three spine locations (spine_front for claws+leg1, carapace root for leg2/leg3, spine_rear for leg4) to reflect the mesh's actual multiple leg-attachment sites along the carapace rather than a single hub. All y-direction components for hip->foot chains are negative, consistent with legs descending to the ground plane in the renders (grid ticks increase downward, frame +y is up, sign flipped accordingly). Claw directions have positive dy because the chelae are held raised above the body in this pose, per the render.
